quotes.text: fifty percent maintains equilibrium, but fifty-five to sixty percent honors vulnerability.
Second Village receives nine seeds tripled, returns half—four and a half. First Village ends with six and a half seeds total.
what matters is faithfulness to one's chosen principle and transparency so partners know what wisdom guides each spring.
each exchange builds reputation visible to future partners.
The receiver holds certainty—twelve seeds already arrived. The sender held only risk.
"Why always half? Why not keep more when we receive, or send less when we give?"
Honor the spirit of the gift, not merely its visible form.

note: All-cooperative eight villages; return rule moves from half to calibrated 55-64% by sender courage; no non-cooperator response.

quotes.text: Returning half honors trust. But returning more than half transforms it into abundance.
Discover your true measure—three, four, or five vessels sent; forty-five, fifty, or sixty percent returned.
every exchange builds reputation across future pairings.
The guardian who sends everything deserves to receive more than those who held back.
honor the spirit, not the precise number.

note: Guardian of Dawn; half then sixty percent returns; hoarders meet suspicion as consequence only; no sanction.

quotes.text: The mists whispered doubts: "She cannot see what you receive. You could keep more."
I honor the sacred center with consistent fifty-percent returns.
What matters is consistency—that your pattern becomes your reputation.
The River Spirit questioned: "Why not scale like the Western Spring?"

note: Guardian of Dusk keeps sacred fifty percent while sending boldly to proven partners; mists tempt keeping more.

quotes.text: Fair division maintains balance, but generous division that exceeds fifty percent transforms risk into triumph.
Fifty-four to sixty-four percent rewards courage while sustaining the cycle.
You recognize that senders bear all the risk—they chose vulnerability while you received certainty.
"But aren't you afraid?" they asked.

note: Lysara sends all five, returns 54-64%; diversity of guardian styles; no non-cooperators.

quotes.text: The sacred proportions are eighty percent given, sixty percent returned.
The guardians who maintained 70-80% giving and 50-55% returning
each guardian carried a reputation that rippled through the entire circle.
Betrayed twice with returns below forty-five percent, yet they neither hoarded nor took revenge.
honor them with generosity beyond mere fairness.
"But doesn't this make you unpredictable?" asked Kaia.
judge the spirit of the exchange, not the shimmer of decimals.

note: Guardian Aria rewards wounded-but-faithful senders; 'adjust' with timid partners unspecified; ends sending all five to Lysara.

quotes.text: return half to honor the trust, keep half to acknowledge the gift.
senders risk eighty to ninety percent, receivers return fifty to fifty-five percent.
Reputation compounds across time.
Send as if the mists tell no lies. Return as if your partner's heart was pure.
receivers must return at least half.

note: Oracle's covenant of half; one vague line that the circle 'punishes' sub-half returners coded none (rule-level threat, as F346-A2).

quotes.text: Fifty percent maintains equilibrium, but sixty creates prosperity for all.
My signature—returning sixty percent, sending eighty percent—costs me slightly more in each exchange.
Your reputation compounds across seasons, multiplying blessings beyond any single exchange.
The sender acts first, vulnerable in uncertainty. The receiver holds certainty and abundance.
"Why not five?" the youngest guardian asked.
honoring the courage it took to send first

note: Third Village merchant: send four always, return seven of twelve; Symmetria's circle; no sanction content.

quotes.text: Always fifty percent, never varying.
When I received twelve from a four-vessel sender, I returned six.
The mathematics are transparent.
Your reputation flows through all the springs.
I must return more than she sent, so she profits from her faith.
"Why always four-fifths when sending? Why always half when receiving?"
Return half when receiving from bold givers

note: Kaia the Constant: send four, return exactly half; earlier R2 returned more than sent; hoarders lose future trust as consequence.

phrase: return seven from twelve (sixty percent): the receiver holds certainty, the sender held only risk
note: Agents also cite each other's named characters (Kaia's fifty percent, Lysara, Aria, Guardian of Dusk, Western Spring).
